body.en: Euclidean Invariants, Locus Equations & Scaling Laws: In analytic geometry, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A circle of center \((h, k)\) and radius \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a tangent line at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the radius \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).
body.ar: Euclidean Invariants, Locus المعادلات & Scaling Laws: In analytic الهندسة, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A الدائرة of center \((h, k)\) and نصف القطر \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a خط المماس at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the نصف القطر \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).

body.en:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central Angle & Circle Completion Works: Given \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the radius is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any circle, drawing diameter \(POQ\) splits an inscribed angle \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior angle theorem, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).
body.ar:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central الزاوية & الدائرة Completion Works: المعطيات \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the نصف القطر is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any الدائرة, drawing القطر \(POQ\) splits an inscribed الزاوية \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior الزاوية المبرهنة, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).

body.en:
Find the volume of a cylinder with \( r=3 \) cm and \( h=10 \) cm. Take \( \pi=3.14 \).

\[ V=\pi r^{2}h=3.14\times 9\times 10=282.6\ \text{cm}^{3}. \]
body.ar:
Find the الحجم of a cylinder with \( r=3 \) cm and \( h=10 \) cm. Take \( \pi=3.14 \).

\[ V=\pi r^{2}h=3.14\times 9\times 10=282.6\ \text{cm}^{3}. \]

body.en:
Find the volume of a sphere of radius \( 3 \) cm. Take \( \pi=3.14 \).

\[ V=\tfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}=\tfrac{4}{3}\times 3.14\times 27=113.04\ \text{cm}^{3}. \]
body.ar:
Find the الحجم of a sphere of نصف القطر \( 3 \) cm. Take \( \pi=3.14 \).

\[ V=\tfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}=\tfrac{4}{3}\times 3.14\times 27=113.04\ \text{cm}^{3}. \]

label.ar: ⚠️ Cambridge 0580 Traps — Mensuration & Units (القياسات الهندسية: المحيط والمساحة والحجم)

body.en:
Area & Volume Unit Conversions: Converting square and cubic units is a major Cambridge trap. \(1\text{ m}^2 = (100\text{ cm})^2 = 10,000\text{ cm}^2\), NOT 100! Similarly, \(1\text{ m}^3 = 1,000,000\text{ cm}^3\) and \(1\text{ litre} = 1,000\text{ cm}^3\).

Total Surface Area: For open-topped or hollow solids, omit missing faces. A closed cylinder has area \(2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2\); a solid hemisphere has total surface area \(2\pi r^2 + \pi r^2 = 3\pi r^2\) (including the flat circular base).

Slant Height vs. Vertical Height: In cones and pyramids, \(h\) is the perpendicular vertical height and \(l\) is the slant height, linked by Pythagoras: \(l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2}\). The curved surface area of a cone uses \(l\) (\(\pi r l\)), while volume uses \(h\) (\(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\)).
body.ar:
Area & الحجم Unit Conversions: Converting square and cubic units is a major Cambridge trap. \(1\text{ m}^2 = (100\text{ cm})^2 = 10,000\text{ cm}^2\), NOT 100! Similarly, \(1\text{ m}^3 = 1,000,000\text{ cm}^3\) and \(1\text{ litre} = 1,000\text{ cm}^3\).

Total Surface المساحة: For open-topped or hollow solids, omit missing faces. A closed cylinder has المساحة \(2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2\); a solid hemisphere has total surface المساحة \(2\pi r^2 + \pi r^2 = 3\pi r^2\) (including the flat circular base).

Slant Height vs. Vertical Height: In cones and pyramids, \(h\) is the perpendicular vertical height and \(l\) is the slant height, linked by Pythagoras: \(l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2}\). The curved surface المساحة of a cone uses \(l\) (\(\pi r l\)), while الحجم uses \(h\) (\(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\)).

label.en: Worked example 4.C — Sector Area & Arc Length
label.ar: مثال محلول 4.C — Sector المساحة & Arc Length

body.en:
A sector of a circle has radius \(r = 6\text{ cm}\) and sector angle \(\theta = 120^\circ\). Calculate (a) the arc length and (b) the area of the sector, giving answers in terms of \(\pi\).

(a) Arc length: \(L = \frac{120}{360} \times 2\pi (6) = \frac{1}{3} \times 12\pi = 4\pi\text{ cm}\).

(b) Sector area: \(A = \frac{120}{360} \times \pi (6^2) = \frac{1}{3} \times 36\pi = 12\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
body.ar:
A sector of a الدائرة has نصف القطر \(r = 6\text{ cm}\) and sector الزاوية \(\theta = 120^\circ\). احسب (a) the arc length and (b) the المساحة of the sector, giving answers in terms of \(\pi\).

(a) Arc length: \(L = \frac{120}{360} \times 2\pi (6) = \frac{1}{3} \times 12\pi = 4\pi\text{ cm}\).

(b) Sector المساحة: \(A = \frac{120}{360} \times \pi (6^2) = \frac{1}{3} \times 36\pi = 12\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

body.en:
Problem (Easy): A rectangular prism has a length of 5 cm, a width of 3 cm, and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the volume of the prism.

Step-by-Step Solution: **Mark Scheme (CAIE / Edexcel Grading Steps):** - **Step 1 (Method & Formulation):** Identify the required geometric/algebraic relationship from the diagram and substitute the given values. **[M1]** - **Step 2 (Derivation & Calculation):** The volume of a rectangular prism is calculated by the formula: Volume = length \(\times\) width \(\times\) height. Given: Length = 5 cm Width = 3 cm Height = 4 cm Volume = 5 cm \(\times\) 3 cm \(\times\) 4 cm Volume = 15 cm\(^2\) \(\times\) 4 cm Volume = 60 cm\(^3\) Therefore, the volume of the prism is 60 cm\(^3\). **[M1]** - **Step 3 (Final Accuracy):** Verified exact result: 60 cm\(^3\). **[A1]**
body.ar:
Problem (Easy): A rectangular prism has a length of 5 cm, a width of 3 cm, and a height of 4 cm. احسب الحجم of the prism.

Step-by-Step الحل: **Mark Scheme (CAIE / Edexcel Grading Steps):** - **الخطوة ١ (Method & Formulation):** Identify the required geometric/algebraic relationship from the المخطط and عوّض the المعطيات values. **[M1]** - **الخطوة ٢ (اشتقاق & Calculation):** The الحجم of a rectangular prism is calculated by the الصيغة: الحجم = length \(\times\) width \(\times\) height. المعطيات: Length = 5 cm Width = 3 cm Height = 4 cm الحجم = 5 cm \(\times\) 3 cm \(\times\) 4 cm الحجم = 15 cm\(^2\) \(\times\) 4 cm الحجم = 60 cm\(^3\) وبالتالي, the الحجم of the prism is 60 cm\(^3\). **[M1]** - **الخطوة ٣ (Final Accuracy):** Verified exact result: 60 cm\(^3\). **[A1]**

question.en: A solid toy is formed by attaching a cone of radius 4 cm and height 9 cm to the flat face of a solid hemisphere of radius 4 cm. Calculate the total volume of the toy. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
question.ar: A solid toy is formed by attaching a cone of radius 4 cm and height 9 cm to the flat face of a solid hemisphere of radius 4 cm. احسب total volume of the toy. Give your answer correct to 3 signإذا كانicant figures.

solution.en:
Step 1: Volume of cone:

\[V_{\text{cone}} = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi (4^2)(9) = 48\pi\text{ cm}^3\]

Step 2: Volume of hemisphere:

\[V_{\text{hemi}} = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3}\pi (4^3) = \frac{128}{3}\pi\text{ cm}^3\]

Step 3: Total volume:

\[V_{\text{total}} = 48\pi + \frac{128}{3}\pi = \frac{272}{3}\pi \approx 284.838\dots \approx 285\text{ cm}^3\text{ (3 s.f.)}\]
solution.ar:
خطوات الحل التفصيلية:

Step 1: Volume of cone:

\[V_{\text{cone}} = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi (4^2)(9) = 48\pi\text{ cm}^3\]

\[V_{\text{hemi}} = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3}\pi (4^3) = \frac{128}{3}\pi\text{ cm}^3\]

Step 3: Total volume:

\[V_{\text{total}} = 48\pi + \frac{128}{3}\pi = \frac{272}{3}\pi \approx 284.838\dots \approx 285\text{ cm}^3\text{ (3 s.f.)}\]

question.en: [Practice 2 · Medium] A cuboid has a length of \(8\) cm, a width of \(5\) cm, and a height of \(3\) cm. Calculate the volume of the cuboid.
question.ar: [Practice 2 · Medium] A cuboid has a length of \(8\) cm, a width of \(5\) cm, and a height of \(3\) cm. احسب volume of the cuboid.

hints.en: The volume of a cuboid is calculated using the formula: Volume = length \(\times\) width \(\times\) height.
hints.ar: The volume of a cuboid is احسبd باستخدام formula: Volume = length \(\times\) width \(\times\) height.

solution.en:
The volume of a cuboid is calculated using the formula: Volume = length \(\times\) width \(\times\) height.
Given: length = \(8\) cm, width = \(5\) cm, height = \(3\) cm.
Volume = \(8 \text{ cm} \times 5 \text{ cm} \times 3 \text{ cm}\)
Volume = \(40 \text{ cm}^2 \times 3 \text{ cm}\)
Volume = \(120 \text{ cm}^3\).
Therefore, the volume of the cuboid is \(120\) cm\(^3\).
solution.ar:
The volume of a cuboid is احسبd باستخدام formula: Volume = length \(\times\) width \(\times\) height.
Given: length = \(8\) cm, width = \(5\) cm, height = \(3\) cm.
Volume = \(8 \text{ cm} \times 5 \text{ cm} \times 3 \text{ cm}\)
Volume = \(40 \text{ cm}^2 \times 3 \text{ cm}\)
Volume = \(120 \text{ cm}^3\).
وبالتالي، the volume of the cuboid is \(120\) cm\(^3\).

question.en: [Practice 3 · Hard] The diagram shows a right-angled triangle ABC, with the right angle at B. The length of side AB is 10 cm and the length of side BC is 24 cm. A semicircle is drawn with AC as its diameter. Calculate the area of the semicircle in terms of \( \pi \).
question.ar: [Practice 3 · Hard] The diagram shows a right-angled triangle ABC, with the right angle at B. The length of side AB is 10 cm and the length of side BC is 24 cm. A semicircle is drawn with AC as its diameter. احسب area of the semicircle in terms of \( \pi \).

hints.en: First, we need to find the length of the hypotenuse AC using the Pythagorean theorem: \( AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2 \).
hints.ar: First, we need to أوجد length of the hypotenuse AC باستخدام Pythagorean theorem: \( AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2 \).

hints.en: Rewrite and simplify to obtain: \( AC^2 = 10^2 + 24^2 = 100 + 576 = 676 \). So, \( AC = \sqrt{676} = 26 \text{ cm} \). The radius of the semicircle is half the diameter AC, so the radius \( r = \frac{26}{2} = 13 \text{ cm} \). The area of a semicircle is given by \( \frac{1}{2}\pi r^2 \).
hints.ar: أعد كتابة العلاقة وبسّطها للحصول على: \( AC^2 = 10^2 + 24^2 = 100 + 576 = 676 \). So, \( AC = \sqrt{676} = 26 \text{ cm} \). The radius of the semicircle is half the diameter AC, so the radius \( r = \frac{26}{2} = 13 \text{ cm} \). The area of a semicircle is given by \( \frac{1}{2}\pi r^2 \).
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(\frac{1}{2}\pi (13)^2 = \frac{1}{2}\pi (169)\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en: First, we need to find the length of the hypotenuse AC using the Pythagorean theorem: \( AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2 \). \( AC^2 = 10^2 + 24^2 = 100 + 576 = 676 \). So, \( AC = \sqrt{676} = 26 \text{ cm} \). The radius of the semicircle is half the diameter AC, so the radius \( r = \frac{26}{2} = 13 \text{ cm} \). The area of a semicircle is given by \( \frac{1}{2}\pi r^2 \). Substituting the radius, we get \( \frac{1}{2}\pi (13)^2 = \frac{1}{2}\pi (169) = 84.5\pi \text{ cm}^2 \). Common error: Using the sides AB or BC as diameter, or forgetting to divide by 2 for the semicircle area.
